scope: Experimental SIM-6A two-domain frictionless node-to-surface penalty contact with small sliding, linear penalty normal behavior, no initial adjustment, and bounded quasi-static increments.

lanes.acceptance: The v2 contract admits only the declared two-domain frictionless small-sliding envelope and rejects missing capability profiles, invalid increment bounds, stale identity, and incompatible contact geometry.

The CalculiX adapter emits deterministic face-based secondary/primary surfaces, SMALL SLIDING contact, linear pressure-overclosure, bounded *STATIC increments, and final CDIS/CSTR output without friction or automatic adjustment.

evidence.contactCard: *CONTACT PAIR, TYPE=NODE TO SURFACE, SMALL SLIDING

lanes.acceptance: Bounded FRD and STA parsers reject invalid magnitudes and incomplete increment histories; request-aware normalization bounds CalculiX's small tensile regularizer, preserves signed COPEN, recovers omitted-node clearance against a planar primary, and retains interface ownership, pressure/gap datasets, slip, resultant force, and final step time.

A real Gmsh/CalculiX planar patch fixture demonstrates the expected approximately uniform pressure plus global and contact-force equilibrium. Refinement and penalty trends remain isolated in their own required lane.
Independent real solves demonstrate active closing under compressive loading and complete opening under prescribed tensile separation without tensile contact traction.

A deformable half-cylinder on a planar foundation demonstrates a center-high, edge-decaying Hertz-type pressure strip, contracting peak-pressure changes under refinement, fine-mesh contact width agreement, exact secondary-body force equilibrium, and reduced bounded penetration under a stiffer penalty.

evidence.fixture: R10 x 10 mm half-cylinder on planar steel foundation

lanes.acceptance: Deliberate cutback exhaustion and cancellation fixtures fail closed, terminate descendants, clean native files, and return no partial engineering result.
An independent qualified engineer approves the formulation, fixtures, tolerances, sign conventions, assumptions, and exact reviewed commit.
